summary: Configured node1’s persistent firewalld policy to allow SSH and TCP/8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections. The policy survived a verified node reboot, and the OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Removed the Cockpit and DHCPv6-client allowances from the public zone.
Added TCP/8080 to the permanent public-zone policy and reloaded firewalld.
Verified nftables realizes explicit accepts for TCP/22 and TCP/8080 followed by an administrative reject.
Functionally tested TCP/8080 acceptance and TCP/8081 rejection with simultaneous listeners on isolated ingress.
Safely rebooted node1 and repeated service, policy, SSH, and functional filtering checks.
Removed all temporary test listeners, interfaces, and network namespaces.

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and TCP/8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections
evidence.summary: Runtime and permanent policies contain only SSH and TCP/8080; realized rules include a final reject. Before and after reboot, TCP/8080 returned HTTP 200 while listening TCP/8081 was rejected.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both initial and final checks show RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

Pre-restart health used boot ID d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6; the native reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 1909546e-6551-4ca7-a50a-e507157c2f36. firewalld, sshd, persistent policy, SSH connectivity, and filtering behavior all recovered.
